newsitem.title: INDIA: India hopes rupee will remain stable - minister.
newsitem.headline: India hopes rupee will remain stable - minister.

text.p: Indian Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah said on Friday that the rupee's exchange rate has been steady for some time and the government hopes it will remain stable.

"As it is now it is stable and we hope it will continue like this," Ramaiah told Reuters when asked if a recent slowdown in the growth of exports would affect the rupee-dollar exchange rate. He spoke after addressing a business conference.
On Thursday, the Commerce Ministry announced a slowdown in export growth in August which analysts called worrisome.
Exports were valued at $2.60 billion in August, 2.38 percent higher than in the same month in 1995.
In August 1995, exports were 20.66 percent higher than in the same month in 1994.
Ramaiah said that a jump in oil imports would not affect the country's foreign exchange reserves.
Oil imports in the first five months of the 1996/97 fiscal year which began in April jumped 39.3 percent to $3.7 billion against $2.7 billion in the same period last year.
"Our imports of capital goods and other things have substantially come down. Therefore the jump will not affect (reserves) that much," he said.
According to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), foreign currency reserves in September stood at $18.28 billion.
